concepts.name: Supervised learning pipeline
concepts.summary: The steps from problem framing and data splits through training, evaluation and deployment.

concepts.name: Loss function vs evaluation metric
concepts.summary: A loss scores one prediction for training; a metric summarizes performance for decisions.

concepts.name: Expected risk
concepts.summary: The average loss of a model over the unknown data-generating distribution.

concepts.name: Empirical risk
concepts.summary: The average loss on the training set, used as a practical stand-in for expected risk.

concepts.name: Squared (L2) vs absolute (L1) loss
concepts.summary: Squared loss penalizes large errors quadratically and is more sensitive to outliers than absolute loss.

concepts.name: 1D linear regression and residuals
concepts.summary: Fit a line with weight and bias so that residuals between predictions and targets are small.

concepts.name: Cost surface in weight space and convexity
concepts.summary: For linear regression the squared-loss cost is a convex quadratic bowl over the weights, so any local minimum is global.

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.summary: Repeatedly step the weights against the gradient of the cost, scaled by a learning rate.

concepts.name: Multivariate linear regression (vectorized, bias trick)
concepts.summary: Stack examples into a design matrix and add a column of ones so predictions are a single matrix product.

concepts.name: Normal equation (closed-form solution)
concepts.summary: Setting the gradient of the cost to zero gives w = (X^T X)^-1 X^T y when X^T X is invertible.

concepts.name: Nonlinear regression with feature maps
concepts.summary: Map inputs through features such as polynomials so a model linear in its parameters can fit nonlinear curves.

concepts.name: Underfitting, overfitting and validation error
concepts.summary: As model complexity grows, training error keeps falling while validation error has a sweet spot.

concepts.name: 0-1 loss and logistic (cross-entropy) loss
concepts.summary: 0-1 loss is intuitive but not differentiable; cross-entropy is smooth and punishes confident mistakes.

concepts.name: Why linear regression is a bad classifier
concepts.summary: Regressing on 0/1 labels gives predictions outside [0,1] and a loss that ignores the Bernoulli structure.
